title: Financing Infrastructure After LGFVs

Financing Infrastructure After LGFVs

Xiaoxi Zhang

Gavekal Dragonomics | 20 Nov 2026

The math for financing infrastructure projects doesn’t work anymore. For years, China’s local governments have relied on a combination of public, on-balance-sheet financing and hidden, off-balance-sheet funding to deliver high volumes of investment without blowing up their official debt numbers. But the repeated bailouts of local government financing vehicles’ (LGFVs) hidden debts have made the central government wary of this model, and it has been gradually curtailing off-balance-sheet financing.Those curbs have built up over time, and are now materially constraining infrastructure spending. Fixed-asset investment in infrastructure sectors is down 7.3% in the year through October, with the decline deepening in recent months despite government pledges to stabilize investment. The reality is that the financial returns on infrastructure projects remain too low to attract private-sector investors. That leaves the government with an unpleasant trade-off: either pay for infrastructure projects entirely with government bonds, and accept rising debt, or allow infrastructure investment to keep declining, and accept weaker growth. It is choosing the latter.
